examined_scientific_unknowns.question: Worker effects across institutional and work-design settings
examined_scientific_unknowns.current_conclusion: Adverse and favorable evidence differ in design and perspective; no universal causal verdict.
examined_scientific_unknowns.discriminator: A better identified comparison with worker-centered outcomes and meaningful alternative explanations.

examined_scientific_unknowns.question: Economical resilience under correlated disruption
examined_scientific_unknowns.current_conclusion: Information and contingent buffer/alternative choices are useful hypotheses; no universal optimum or causal package effect.
examined_scientific_unknowns.discriminator: Measured common-cause exposure, feasible alternatives and a comparative outcome design.

examined_scientific_unknowns.question: Comparative set-based benefit and option carrying cost
examined_scientific_unknowns.current_conclusion: Conceptual and case support does not establish universal superiority.
examined_scientific_unknowns.discriminator: Comparable projects with uncertainty, coupling, integration and cost measured.

examined_scientific_unknowns.question: Historical transmission of particular software mechanisms
examined_scientific_unknowns.current_conclusion: Explicit translations are documented; direct Lean ancestry of every modern mechanism is unproved.
examined_scientific_unknowns.discriminator: Dated primary transmission records for each asserted mechanism.

examined_scientific_unknowns.question: Domain outcome durability and causal attribution
examined_scientific_unknowns.current_conclusion: Process changes do not by themselves identify beneficiary benefit; co-interventions and overlapping studies remain.
examined_scientific_unknowns.discriminator: Better controlled primary outcome data with exposure and estimand preserved.
